citations.narrative:
Two adult rabbits were housed in the same primary enclosure as 1 capybara, 1 patagonian cavy, 1 cape porcupine, and 1
alpaca. These animals were being exhibited as a petting zoo on August 9, 2026 at a local mall. A brief video of this
exhibition was submitted and shown to the licensee. The licensee indicated that these rabbits were not separated from
the other species at this event. Housing rabbits with other species may result in injury or compatibility issues. Correct by
ensuring rabbits are not housed in the same primary enclosure with any other species of animals unless required for
scientific reasons.
Correct by October 27, 2026.

citations.desc: Primary enclosures used to transport live animals.
citations.narrative:
The primary enclosures used to transport animals for exhibition do not have the appropriate marking and labeling required
for transporting live animals. Accurately labeled enclosures allow for proper handling and care. For animal safety, unless
the enclosures are permanently affixed to the conveyance, primary enclosures must be clearly marked on top and on one
or more sides with the words “Live Animals” or “Wild Animals” in letters at least 1 inch (2.5 cm.) in height, and with arrows
or other markings to indicate the correct upright position of the container.
Correct by October 27, 2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the licensee.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
